blocks.text: 14 November 2026. North Seymour and Las Bachas or South Plaza and Punta Carrión
The boat excursion is included. You'll follow one of the two routes, confirmed after booking. Both islands are equally rewarding to visit.
Option 1: North Seymour and Las Bachas

Today's excursion takes you to North Seymour Island and the beaches of Las Bachas.
Take a bus to the yacht in the Itabaca Channel, then sail for an hour to North Seymour Island.
You'll land on a rocky shore near a small grove of gray and silver palo santo trees, which are leafless for most of the year.
North Seymour is known for its many bird colonies. Look out for male frigatebirds, which inflate their red throat pouches to attract females during mating season, and for the famous blue-footed boobies. These seabirds have wedge-shaped tails and long, pointed wings. During courtship, the males lift a wing and a blue foot as they dance to impress the females. The excursion continues along a beach with low cliffs, where you can see gulls, numerous sea lions, marine iguanas and pelicans. Many of the animals can be seen at close range.
A freshly prepared lunch is served aboard the yacht.
As you relax after lunch, the yacht sails to Las Bachas on the north coast of Santa Cruz Island. First, walk to the lagoon behind the beach, which flamingos often visit. Then swim and snorkel off an uninhabited white-sand beach with turquoise water. You may encounter sea lions, several kinds of rays, sea turtles and tropical fish in the water.
Return to Puerto Ayora at around 4:00 p.m. Enjoy free time to stroll along the pier, shop for souvenirs or watch the sunset.
